- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–25% to compensate for bearish bias.
- After a sharp spike in price (true outcome > 5x recent mean), model often overreacts and forecasts too high; cap forecast at 2x recent peak or use moving average to smooth.
- Model consistently underestimates long-term (30d) trends when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; apply a 15–20% upward bias for 10–15 day horizons.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome exceeds 3x historical 30d mean, model often fails to capture momentum; apply exponential smoothing with decay factor 0.8 to recent true values.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of lagged sentiment to forecast weights for better alignment.
